findings.title: Cached translations not invalidated when SiteSetting.default_locale changes
findings.body: The `translate` method in `translate_accelerator.rb` caches results using a key of `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. When a translation is missing in the user's locale, the fallback chain (which includes `SiteSetting.default_locale`) is used to resolve it, and the result is cached. If an admin later changes `SiteSetting.default_locale` at runtime, previously cached translations will still reflect the old fallback locale until the LRU cache evicts them or the process restarts. The cache key should incorporate the default locale, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale setting changes.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList extends Hash but never populates it
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList` inherits from `Hash` but overrides `[]` to always compute a fresh array without ever storing entries. This means any code that relies on standard Hash behavior (e.g., `each`, `keys`, `key?`, `fetch`, or serialization) will see an empty hash. If the `i18n` gem or any middleware ever calls a method other than `[]` on `I18n.fallbacks`, it will get unexpected results. Consider inheriting from `Object` instead, or documenting that only `[]` and `ensure_loaded!` are supported.

findings.title: Non-atomic `@loaded_locales ||= []` in ensure_loaded!
findings.body: In a multi-threaded server (e.g., Puma), two threads could both observe `@loaded_locales` as `nil`, each create a new empty array, and one assignment silently overwrites the other. While `load_locale` is mutex-protected, the check-then-load pattern in `ensure_loaded!` (`@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` followed by `load_locale`) is not atomic with respect to `reload!` setting `@loaded_locales = []`. A thread could pass the `include?` check, then `reload!` resets the array, and the thread proceeds to call `load_locale` which re-adds the locale to the fresh array — benign in this case, but the `||=` initialization is a data race under the Ruby memory model.

findings.title: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` called on every request
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` iterates over all fallback locales (up to 3) and checks `@loaded_locales.include?` for each on every request, even when locales are already loaded. This is a minor per-request overhead. Consider a fast-path check (e.g., a flag or comparing against a cached set) to skip the iteration when nothing has changed, or move the call to only trigger when the locale actually changes from the previous value.
